title: Weather widget
summary: Recreate a widget: a gradient card, a sun peeking behind a cloud, a big light temperature and a four-day row.
brief: The card has 20px corners, white text, a 160deg gradient from #38bdf8 to #6366f1 and a soft indigo shadow (0 12px 30px rgb(99 102 241 / 0.35)).

Top row (icon and reading), vertically centred and 16px apart. The icon is an 80 × 64px area: a 44px yellow (#fde047) glowing sun in its top right corner (4px in from the right), and in front of it a white cloud: a 64 × 30px pill on the bottom left with a 30px bump 14px from its left, 12px above its bottom.
The temperature is 56px with weight 200 and line-height 1; the line under it is 13px at 85% opacity.

The forecast is 20px below: four equal columns 8px apart. Each day is a tile with a 18% white background, 12px corners, 10px padding above and below, its name over its temperature (semibold), centred, 4px apart.
hints: The top row is flex with align-items: center. Inside .icon (position: relative) the sun and the cloud are position: absolute, and the cloud comes later in the page, so it is drawn in front of the sun.
The cloud’s bump is .cloud::before: a 30px white circle, absolutely positioned with bottom: 12px and left: 14px inside the cloud (which is already positioned).
The forecast is display: grid with grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr). Each .day is a small grid with justify-items: center. A see-through tile is background-color: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.18).
solutionNotes: Three small systems: a flex row for the icon and reading, a 4-column grid for the forecast, and an absolutely positioned drawing inside a fixed-size icon box. Paint order does the layering in the icon: both shapes are positioned, so the later one (the cloud) is drawn over the sun without any z-index, and the cloud’s ::before bump belongs to the cloud so it is in front too. Thin weights at huge sizes look elegant; the translucent white tiles pick up the gradient behind them instead of hiding it.
